tasks.title: Rate-limit SMS sends (429) on enroll + challenge
tasks.description: Add a per-factor minimum-resend-interval rate limit to the TWO SMS send paths in backend/app/services/mfa.py: MfaEnrollmentService._prepare_sms (the re-arm path reached via POST /auth/mfa/enrollments) and MfaChallengeService.issue (POST /auth/mfa/challenges). GOAL: bound SMS sends to at most one per cooldown window per factor, closing the SMS-cost/bombing vector. NON-NEGOTIABLE DESIGN (migration-free): do NOT add a DB column and do NOT create an Alembic migration. Derive the last-send instant from the EXISTING column as last_sent_at = sms_challenge_expires_at - SMS_CHALLENGE_TTL (only when sms_challenge_expires_at is not None). If a prior challenge exists and _utc_now() - last_sent_at < SMS_RESEND_INTERVAL, refuse BEFORE calling self._sms.send_verification_code. Requirements: (1) add a constant SMS_RESEND_INTERVAL = datetime.timedelta(seconds=60) in backend/app/auth/mfa.py next to SMS_CHALLENGE_TTL, with a comment; SMS_RESEND_INTERVAL must be < SMS_CHALLENGE_TTL. (2) add a new exception class SmsRateLimited(MfaServiceError) with status_code=429, code='RATE_LIMITED', a clear message; raise it from both send paths. (3) The FIRST send for a factor (no prior challenge: existing is None on enroll, or sms_challenge_expires_at is None) MUST always be allowed — never rate-limit a first send. (4) On the challenge path keep the existing 423 lockout check FIRST (a locked factor stays 423, not 429); the rate-limit check comes after the lock check but before the send. (5) The rate limit must NOT reset or touch failed_attempts/locked_at (same discipline as the lockout — re-issuing never clears a lock). (6) Declare the new 429 response on BOTH operations (createMfaEnrollment, createMfaChallenge) in backend/openapi/paths/ep1-identity.yaml, reusing the existing Error schema/response component the other statuses use (reachable statuses must be declared — same rule applied to the earlier 502 declarations). (7) Add tests to backend/tests/test_mfa_enrollment.py (or a sibling) proving: a first SMS enroll/challenge succeeds; an immediate second send returns 429 with code RATE_LIMITED and does NOT deliver a second SMS (assert the MockSmsSender recorded only one code); a send after the interval elapses succeeds (advance time by monkeypatching the service clock / _utc_now or by ageing sms_challenge_expires_at in the DB — do NOT sleep); a TOTP enroll is unaffected; a locked factor on the challenge path still returns 423 (not 429). ACCEPTANCE: full backend suite green in your isolated checkout; .softhouse/verify-docs.sh does not regress; check_models, check_migration (must STILL show offline metadata == migration, i.e. NO new migration), openapi/validate.py, and pytest all PASS — run all of them before finishing. Scope is strictly these files.

tasks.title: Independent review of the SMS rate-limit
tasks.description: INDEPENDENT adversarial review of T1. You did not plan it; assume defects exist. Read CLAUDE.md, .softhouse/patterns.md, the T1 handoff at .softhouse/handoff/20260805-sms-ratelimit/T1.md, and git diff main..<T1 branch>. VERIFY BY PROBING, not by reading: (1) The first send is genuinely never rate-limited — both a brand-new enrollment AND a re-send after the prior challenge has EXPIRED (check the last_sent_at = expires_at - TTL arithmetic at the boundary; an off-by-one that blocks a legitimate post-expiry resend is a defect). (2) A second send inside the window is blocked BEFORE self._sms.send_verification_code is called — no SMS leaves on the 429 path (a 429 that still sends is worthless). (3) SMS_RESEND_INTERVAL < SMS_CHALLENGE_TTL holds; reason about a challenge that is live but older than the interval (resend allowed, overwrites — acceptable) vs younger (blocked). (4) The rate limit does not touch failed_attempts/locked_at and cannot reset a lockout; the challenge-path lock check still precedes it and still 423s. (5) NO new DB column and NO new migration (check_migration must still pass; git diff shows no migrations/ change). (6) The 429 is declared on both operations in the OpenAPI contract and openapi/validate.py passes. (7) No money/ledger touched; no non-negotiable weakened. (8) The clock is injectable/monkeypatchable in tests without sleeping, and the tests actually assert the single-delivery property (not just the status code). Re-run .softhouse/verify-docs.sh + the four code gates against the branch. Report each finding as severity / location / what is wrong / the fix. Verdict: APPROVED, MICRO-FIX (<=10 lines mechanical), or REJECTED with specifics. If you find nothing, say what you checked so silence is distinguishable from not looking.
